title: Directives, conditional builds and macros
goal: Trace what preprocessing directives do during a build, then switch a packing profile without changing the program's input.

prerequisites.text: Recall int, multiplication, and operator precedence. You will use them to predict the result after macro expansion.
Recall the roles of main, a header, and a run. This lesson separates a choice made during the build from input read during the run.

terms.title: Directive
terms.definition: An instruction to the preprocessor. For example, #include brings in the contents of the named header.

terms.title: Macro
terms.definition: A name or pattern that the preprocessor replaces with a sequence of tokens. The resulting expression may still need to be evaluated.

terms.title: Conditional processing
terms.definition: Directives #if, #elif and #else keep only the selected group for further processing. This happens before main runs.

sections.title: The working model
paragraphs: A pickup station uses two shelving profiles. The profile determines the capacity, while input determines the number of groups after launch. A build-time setting is appropriate when the deployment configuration is known in advance and stays fixed for the run.
The #if expression is evaluated by the preprocessor. Its result determines which CAPACITY definition is kept. For an unsupported profile, #error stops the build with the specified diagnostic.
TOTAL(1 + 2) expands to ((1 + 2) * 8). Keep parentheses around a macro parameter and around the full result. Repeating a parameter in a macro can also repeat side effects in its argument.
Changing a macro in a header requires another build. It does not create a switch the running program can read from stdin.

sections.title: Calculate pickup capacity
paragraphs: The header sets DELIVERY_MODE to 1. Predict the capacity of three shelves written as 1 + 2. Leave stdin empty.
steps: First, #include makes the definitions from delivery_policy.h available to the source.
Exactly one branch leaves CAPACITY defined as 8. Predict the selected branch before reading main.
Substitute 1 + 2 into TOTAL without losing the parentheses, then calculate 3 × 8.

files.delivery_policy.h:
#ifndef DELIVERY_POLICY_H
#define DELIVERY_POLICY_H
#define DELIVERY_MODE 1

#if DELIVERY_MODE == 1
#define CAPACITY 8
#elif DELIVERY_MODE == 2
#define CAPACITY 12
#else
#error unsupported DELIVERY_MODE
#endif

#define TOTAL(count) ((count) * CAPACITY)
#endif

sections.title: Identify the failed build stage
paragraphs: Profile 3 in the separate PACK_KIND fixture produces unsupported PACK_KIND before printf can run. Locate #error and restore a supported configuration.
If the program runs with the wrong arithmetic, write out the expanded expression first. Incorrect precedence is a different symptom from a build that stops.

sections.title: Predict, verify, and explain
paragraphs: In a copy of the worked example, change only DELIVERY_MODE from 1 to 2. Predict the full line capacity=12 total=36, then build and compare. Restore 1 and mentally expand TOTAL without its inner parentheses. (1 + 2 * 8) would give 17. Explain the different result.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: The source processing order, conditional directives, and macro replacement.

selfcheck.prompt: You set DELIVERY_MODE to 2 in the example. When can the program show the new result?
options: After entering 2 in stdin of the running program
Immediately on saving the source without a build
feedback: A new build processes the directives again.
Input cannot redefine a directive in an already built program.
Saving source does not change a binary that is already running.

selfcheck.prompt: What does the correct TOTAL(1 + 2) compute with CAPACITY 8?
feedback: 17 would follow if the argument lacked parentheses.
The parentheses force addition before multiplication.
The macro multiplies the group size by 8.

selfcheck.prompt: A learner sees unsupported PACK_KIND. Why does changing stdin not help, and which file should they examine?
selfcheck.feedback: The build diagnosed the problem before running. Check PACK_KIND in packing_config.h against the two supported values, 0 and 1.

files.packing_config.h:
#ifndef PACKING_CONFIG_H
#define PACKING_CONFIG_H
#define PACK_KIND 3

#if PACK_KIND == 0
#define PACK_SIZE 1
#elif PACK_KIND == 1
#define PACK_SIZE 6
#else
#error unsupported PACK_KIND
#endif

#define BOX_AMOUNT(count) ((count) * PACK_SIZE)
#endif

practice.title: Convert boxes into items
practice.task: Profile 1 means 6 items in each box. Select it in packing_config.h and pass boxes to BOX_AMOUNT in main.c. The first line of stdin is exactly one digit followed by LF or end of input. Print items= followed by the number of items for valid input. Otherwise print invalid and exit with code 1.

files.content:
#ifndef PACKING_CONFIG_H
#define PACKING_CONFIG_H
#define PACK_KIND 0

#if PACK_KIND == 0
#define PACK_SIZE 1
#elif PACK_KIND == 1
#define PACK_SIZE 6
#else
#error unsupported PACK_KIND
#endif

#define BOX_AMOUNT(count) ((count) * PACK_SIZE)
#endif

criteria: For 3, 0 and 9 print 18, 0 and 54 with the items= prefix. stderr stays empty.
Two digits or x produce invalid and exit code 1. Use the macro instead of a literal multiplier in main.
practice.hint: Check both changes. The directives select the box size, and main must actually use BOX_AMOUNT.

files.packing_config.h:
#ifndef PACKING_CONFIG_H
#define PACKING_CONFIG_H
#define PACK_KIND 1

#if PACK_KIND == 0
#define PACK_SIZE 1
#elif PACK_KIND == 1
#define PACK_SIZE 6
#else
#error unsupported PACK_KIND
#endif

#define BOX_AMOUNT(count) ((count) * PACK_SIZE)
#endif

steps.why: It prints the box count directly.
The multiplication now follows the build setting.

steps.action: Try 9 with no LF and 10 with LF.
steps.why: One digit is valid. Two digits break the input contract.

exercises.title: Check the earlier profile
exercises.task: In a copy of your solution set PACK_KIND to 0 and run with 3 again. Restore profile 1 afterward.
criteria: Profile 0 prints items=3, while profile 1 prints items=18. Identify the line that selects the value and the line that uses it.

teaching.scene: A warehouse builds the same program for different box sizes. Determine how a build-time selection changes the capacity and the calculation.

predict.prompt: DELIVERY_MODE is 1 in the header, and main calls TOTAL(1 + 2). What line does the program print? Show the replacement expression.
predict.answer: Mode 1 defines CAPACITY as 8. TOTAL(1 + 2) becomes ((1 + 2) * 8). The result is capacity=8 total=24.

apply.prompt: Select DELIVERY_MODE 2 in a copy of the header. Predict both fields after rebuilding, with main.c untouched.
apply.answer: The #elif branch defines CAPACITY as 12. The sum 1 + 2 is multiplied by 12. The result is capacity=12 total=36 after the new build.

practice.strategy: Check which profile the header selects. Then trace how the box count read in main reaches the calculation. Test 3, 0, and a malformed line.
practice.diagnosis: If items is wrong for 3, separate two possibilities: the build selected the other profile or main bypassed the macro. Inspect both files before changing the input rules.

syntax.explanation: The preprocessor replaces sequences of tokens before compilation. Parentheses preserve the intended grouping when an argument is an expression.
syntax.mistake: If TOTAL(count) expands to count * CAPACITY, the input 1 + 2 gives 1 + 2 * 8, or 17. Keep parentheses around both the argument and the replacement.
